model_output.verdict: A store manager with a clear record of sales growth, lower turnover and reduced shrink.
write_up: This is a strong store manager resume! You show the size of the store you run and connect changes you made to sales, turnover and shrink. A recruiter can see both the job and what changed under your management.

The fixed-schedule line is a great model: it names the decision and shows the change in turnover. Your opening mentions turning around two stores, though the work beneath it makes the current store's turnaround much easier to see than the other one.
Let's add a little more about the other store's turnaround, if you can. Your resume isn't the weak link here; competition for a particular store manager job will matter too.

cards.line: Retail store manager who has turned around two underperforming stores in a 60-store regional chain.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see results at your current store, but can't tell what changed at the other store or what part you played in its turnaround. Give that second claim something concrete behind it.
cards.example: Retail store manager who has turned around two underperforming stores in a 60-store regional chain, including [what you did at the other store] and [what changed there].
cards.question: What did you do at the other store, and what changed there?

cards.line: - Cut annual staff turnover from 68% to 41% by moving to fixed weekly schedules
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It puts the before and after next to the scheduling change, so a recruiter doesn't have to guess what you did.
